description: A multi-mode sequencer and voltage generator whose personality changes with the app it is running, giving four triggers and four control voltages

params.text: A key whose job depends on the running app: a long hold opens the time view in Kria and Meadowphysics, a short tap steps to the previous pattern in Earthsea and Levels, and it adds friction in Cycles
A key whose job depends on the app: a long hold opens the config view in Kria, Meadowphysics, Cycles and Levels; a short tap gives the next pattern in Earthsea, a pattern reset in Cycles and Levels
Short-press to open the preset view; press and hold to rotate through the apps available with the connected device, which the lamp beside it shows by colour
Click to reclaim a grid or arc that has been taken by another module; the right-click menu is where a device is first chosen

inputs.text: A trigger input whose job depends on the running app: a clock in Kria, Meadowphysics, Earthsea and Levels, and friction in Cycles
A trigger input whose job depends on the running app: a reset in Kria, Meadowphysics, Cycles and Levels, a pattern start and reset in Earthsea, and force in Cycles when the first input is patched

outputs.text: One of four trigger outputs, 0V low and 8V high, driven by the running app
One of four control outputs, 0V to 10V, driven by the running app

notes: this module does nothing until a grid or an arc is connected. Add a grid 64, grid 128 or grid 256 module, or attach hardware, then right-click here and pick it from the Device Connection list.
the five apps are Kria, Meadowphysics, Earthsea, Cycles and Levels; the first three need a grid, the last two an arc. The hardware MIDI and Teletype expander modes are absent here.
once an app is running the device can be disconnected and the app keeps running, answering the panel keys and the two inputs as before.
the lamp beside the mode key names the running app by colour: yellow-orange is Kria on a grid or Levels on an arc, white is Meadowphysics or Cycles, and yellow-white is Earthsea.
to hold one of the panel keys down with a mouse, control-click it on Windows or Linux and command-click it on a Mac; it stays down until you click it again.
the reset follows the Nord protocol: only a clock edge advances the sequence, and a reset going high makes the next clock step start it again. Delay the clock if a reset misses.
menu: Firmware Tools — opens a submenu naming the firmware and its version, with the input and output rate settings, a screenshot command, and the firmware reload commands
Input rate — sets how often the module reads its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Output rate — sets how often the module writes its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Save PNG screenshot — writes a picture of the module to disk; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Switch Firmware — loads a different firmware build into the module; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Hot Reload — reloads the firmware and keeps both the working memory and the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Reload & Restart — reloads the firmware, discards the working memory and keeps the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Clear NVRAM — wipes the module's stored presets and keeps the working memory; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Device Connection — lists the hardware and virtual grids the module can attach to; pick one to connect it, and the USB jack on the panel then shows a plug in it
